title: Substring of Length K With All Unique Characters
statement: Given a string s and an integer k, return true if there exists a substring of length k containing only unique characters.
think: What is the task asking? Check fixed-size substrings for uniqueness.
What is the key operation? Maintain a moving window and track character counts or membership.
What wording signals stand out? Substring, length k, unique characters.
What is the brute force idea? Build every substring of length k and check uniqueness separately.
What is the better/optimal idea? Slide the window and update counts as characters enter and leave.
What are the edge cases? k = 0, k > s.Length, repeated characters everywhere.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(k) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I maintain a window of size k and track whether all characters inside it are unique.
algorithm: When window size exceeds k, remove left character
Whenever window size == k, check counts.Count == k
interview: I would use a sliding window of size k and track character counts. When the window size is k and the number of distinct characters is also k, the window is fully unique.
ru: Это sliding window: двигаем окно длины k и проверяем, что внутри нет повторов.

important: Forget to remove leaving character from counts
nice: Do not explain why counts.Count == k means all chars are unique

gaps: Important: substring + fixed k => sliding window
Nice to have: distinguish pattern from HashSet used inside
whyThisPattern: This is a Sliding Window problem because we evaluate contiguous substrings of fixed size k while the window moves.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not pure HashSet, because the main pattern is a moving window.
Not Two Pointers, because both pointers define a dynamic contiguous segment rather than comparing ends.
